claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week

  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to ask you some questions about your situation.

**First, let me ask about the child or children you're claiming for:**

What is the age of the child (or children) you want to claim Child Benefit for? Please tell me:
- Their name(s)
- Their age(s) or date(s) of birth

This is important because eligibility rules differ based on whether a child is:
- Under 16 years old
- Between 16-19 years old
- 20 or over

Please share this information and we'll work through the eligibility requirements together.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I'm eligible for Child Benefit. 

I have one child - Alex, who is 9 years old. Can you help me work out if I can claim?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Let me work through the eligibility requirements for your 9-year-old child, Alex.

Since Alex is under 16 years old, that's a good start! Now I need to ask you a few more questions to determine eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question about Alex:**

Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?

Since Alex is only 9 years old, I expect the answer is that Alex is not working, but I need to confirm this as part of the eligibility check.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at all - they're only 9, so they're just in school at the moment!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question:**

Is Alex receiving any benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?

Again, given Alex's age, I expect the answer is no, but I need to confirm this as part of the eligibility requirements.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name. They're just a child living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent, thank you for confirming. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question:**

Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship program?

(This would include apprenticeships in England, Modern Apprenticeships in Scotland, or apprenticeships in Wales - though I expect the answer is no since Alex is only 9 years old and in school.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, not at all - Alex is only 9, so they're just in primary school. No apprenticeships or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me move on to questions about **you** as the claimant.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to ask about your residency status:**

Do you normally live in the UK? 

To meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit, you need to satisfy at least one of the following:
- You normally live in the UK, OR
- You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, OR
- You have pre-settled status and meet certain conditions (working, studying, or have sufficient resources), OR
- You're a Crown servant living abroad

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That satisfies the residency requirement. Now let me ask about your relationship with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question about your relationship with Alex:**

Are you responsible for Alex? This means either:
- You live with Alex, OR
- You contribute to Alex's upkeep (paying for food, clothes, pocket money, housing, etc. - at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount), OR
- You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

From what you've told me (that Alex lives at home with you in Manchester), it sounds like you live with Alex. Can you confirm that?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me here in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question:**

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex? For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- A former partner

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time. If someone else is claiming, you would need to agree between you about who should claim it.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex - it's just me looking after them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question about Alex's living situation:**

Is Alex currently:
- In hospital?
- In local authority care?
- Being fostered?
- Or living normally at home with you?

This is important because there are special rules that apply if a child is in hospital or care for extended periods.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is just living normally at home with me - nothing special like hospital or care or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Final question:**

Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance costs?

(Generally, if the local council is paying for a child's accommodation or upkeep, you cannot claim Child Benefit.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - I'm covering everything for Alex myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me get the final outcome for you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**For Alex (age 9): ELIGIBLE ✓**

You meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex because:
- ✓ Alex is under 16 years old
- ✓ Alex is not in paid work
- ✓ Alex doesn't receive benefits in their own right
- ✓ Alex is not in an apprenticeship
- ✓ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✓ You live with and are responsible for Alex
- ✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- ✓ Alex lives at home with you (not in hospital or care)
- ✓ The local council isn't paying for Alex's care

---

## Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Prepare the following documents:**
   - Proof of your identity
   - Proof of Alex's identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate

3. **Important to know:**
   - Child Benefit is usually paid every 4 weeks
   - If you're a single parent or receive certain benefits, you can choose to be paid weekly

4. **High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   - If you or your partner earn over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay a tax charge
   - The charge applies on a sliding scale between £60,000-£80,000
   - You can still claim Child Benefit but may choose not to receive payments to avoid the charge (while still getting National Insurance credits)

**Ready to apply?** Visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or the application process?

All eligibility criteria are satisfied.
